ios-trial.scope: iPhone-only portrait iOS 17+ technical trial; Android frontmatter tokens and existing component previews remain unchanged.

colorBindings.groupedGround: SwiftUI Form system grouped background, appearance-resolved
colorBindings.rowSurface: SwiftUI Form native row background, appearance-resolved
colorBindings.readableText: Explicit Color(uiColor: .label) for supporting, section, status, error and privacy text; prompt uses foregroundColor(Color(uiColor: .label)). System-resolved, not hierarchical foregroundStyle(.primary).
colorBindings.stopAndWarning: native destructive button role; Color.red warning symbol plus primary text

typeBindings.heading: Font.headline
typeBindings.bodyAndControls: native default body/control styles; Dynamic Type

ios-trial.layout: NavigationStack → scrolling grouped Form; native gutters, row shapes, picker and system sheets. Reading order and enlarged-type scrolling are preserved.
ios-trial.shapesAndIcons: 44pt circular authored mark; native button/row shapes and SF Symbols. Android full-pill and glyph-grid rules do not apply.
ios-trial.states: White play/microphone/progress foreground on Bob Blue. Meaningful status remains visible without a caption. Simulator samples explicitly identify synthetic input.
ios-trial.depthAndMotion: Native platform behavior only; no authored iPhone shadow, veil, halo, pointer or custom motion.
ios-trial.assets: BobMark/AppIcon are deterministic sRGB CoreGraphics renderings of the authored b, with embedded PNG provenance; native sources in ios/Bob/Assets.xcassets.
ios-trial.limitations: Signed iPhone build, installation and trusted physical launch succeeded; Bob and BobBroadcast processes were observed. The first live Settings trial produced no voice according to the user, and a diagnostic build is under investigation. Actual cross-app guidance/playback, background audio, runtime App Group access, extension memory and App Store readiness remain unverified.
ios-trial.status: shelved by user on 2026-11-09; unfinished prototype; Android is the active target

components.name: Help Pill
components.description: The blue pill carrying the hand glyph and its word; side-anchored and snapped to a screen edge.
components.css: .ds-help { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; height: 56px; padding: 0 22px 0 18px; border-radius: 9999px; background: #1F5FE0; color: #fff; border: 1.5px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.9); box-shadow: 0 3px 8px rgba(0,0,0,0.25); font: 700 19px/1.4 Roboto, 'Noto Sans Devanagari', sans-serif; hand: pointer; transition: transform 0.2s cubic-bezier(0.3,0,0.1,1); } .ds-help:hover { transform: translateY(-1px); } .ds-help:active { transform: scale(0.97); } .ds-help:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid #4D8BFF; outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Help Pill, Listening
components.description: The Help pill while the mic is open: near-black with white voice bars and a soft blue halo.
components.css: .ds-help-busy { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; height: 56px; padding: 0 22px 0 18px; border-radius: 9999px; background: #15171C; color: #fff; border: 1.5px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.9); box-shadow: 0 3px 8px rgba(0,0,0,0.25), 0 0 0 6px rgba(31,95,224,0.25); font: 700 19px/1.4 Roboto, sans-serif; } .ds-bars { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 2.8px; width: 24px; height: 24px; } .ds-bars i { display: block; width: 3.2px; border-radius: 2px; background: #fff; height: 12px; animation: ds-bar 1.4s ease-in-out infinite; } .ds-bars i:nth-child(2) { animation-delay: -0.38s; } .ds-bars i:nth-child(3) { animation-delay: -0.76s; } .ds-bars i:nth-child(4) { animation-delay: -1.1s; } @keyframes ds-bar { 0%,100% { height: 8px; } 50% { height: 24px; } } .ds-help-busy:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid #4D8BFF; outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Caption Card

components.css: .ds-caption { background: #15171C; border-radius: 28px; padding: 20px 20px 16px; box-shadow: 0 6px 20px rgba(0,0,0,0.28); font-family: Roboto, 'Noto Sans Devanagari', sans-serif; max-width: 380px; } .ds-cap-head { margin: 0; color: #fff; font-weight: 700; font-size: 24px; line-height: 1.3; } .ds-cap-sub { margin: 6px 0 0; color: rgba(255,255,255,0.7); font-weight: 400; font-size: 18px; line-height: 1.38; } .ds-cap-row { display: flex; gap: 14px; margin-top: 18px; } .ds-pill-repeat, .ds-pill-close { flex: 1; min-height: 56px; padding: 0 16px; border: none; border-radius: 9999px; font: 600 19px/1.4 Roboto, sans-serif; hand: pointer; } .ds-pill-repeat { background: #fff; color: #15171C; } .ds-pill-close { background: rgba(255,255,255,0.16); color: #fff; } .ds-pill-repeat:focus-visible, .ds-pill-close:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid #4D8BFF; outline-offset: 2px; }

narrative.overview:
The incumbent Android system is described below; its numeric frontmatter tokens and overlay/setup rules remain Android-specific. The iPhone technical trial is a native adaptation within this identity, documented explicitly in each relevant section. It does not replace the Android world or imply cross-app overlay support on iOS.

Bob is a pointer and a voice, not a signboard. Over any app, one blue pointing hand flies on an upward arc from the Help pill and lands with its fingertip inside the exact button, then taps it with a ripple; the app is only lightly dimmed and the target sits in a soft rounded spotlight with a faint blue halo. A near-black caption card floats above it all and says the step in white system sans: the first sentence large and bold, the rest smaller at 70% white. Everything the senior might press is a full pill.

The system is clean, modern and calm. Blue is spent only where to press (the hand, the spotlight halo and its tap ripple) and on what can be pressed (the Help pill, the primary pill, a selected tile). The caption is pure contrast, white on near-black, with no grey panels and no borders by day. Setup is the same world on a white ground: one step per screen, five progress segments, a big title, soft grey tiles and one pinned blue pill at the bottom.

The build explicitly refuses the instructional-UI vocabulary of the superseded world: bordered signboards, edge bands and boxy outline buttons.

Bob's spoken voice is the calm male ElevenLabs Eric (`cjVigY5qzO86Huf0OWal`), using `eleven_v3_conversational` across all six app languages. Speech caching and native Android speech fallback support it; speech recognition uses each platform’s native recognizer. The iPhone trial retains Eric with native iPhone speech fallback and uses native controls rather than recreating Android overlays.
keyCharacteristics: The logo is an unmistakable lowercase b: white on Bob Blue, with a tall stem and one clear open counter. The background is flat, with no gradient. Independently authored vector geometry in `branding/bob-mark.svg` supplies the setup mark, adaptive launcher and monochrome themed icon; the Android mark has no font dependency or generated concept raster. iPhone icon/mark assets are deterministic sRGB CoreGraphics rasterizations of that authored geometry, with embedded provenance in `ios/Bob/Assets.xcassets` and renderer `ios/scripts/make-icons.swift`.
One blue pointing hand (48dp, white edge, soft shadow) is the system's in-use mark: pointer and Help pill glyph.
Light veil (22% black by day, 32% at night) with a rounded spotlight; the app stays readable.
Near-black floating caption card, two type sizes ranked by weight and opacity.
Every action is a full pill; containers are softly rounded rectangles (18 to 28dp).
State reads by badge shape (tick, lock, warning) and word, never colour alone.
The phone's own sans (Roboto plus Android's Noto Indic faces), with explicit line heights for Indic scripts.
The iPhone trial uses native SF Dynamic Type, grouped Form surfaces, pickers and SF Symbols; it preserves the blue lowercase b and a single prominent entry action.

rules.name: The Press-Here Rule
rules.body: Outside the approved logo treatment, blue marks only where to press or what can be pressed. Body copy, headings, cards and decoration are never blue.

rules.name: The Pure Contrast Rule
rules.body: The caption is white on near-black. No grey panels, tinted cards or coloured caption backgrounds; rank is carried by size, weight and the 70% white of the second line.

rules.name: The Shape-Not-Hue Rule
rules.body: Every state carries a glyph or word as well as a colour: tick, lock, warning triangle, voice bars, spinning arc, the tick inside a selected tile or segment.

rules.name: The Two Sizes Rule
rules.body: A caption uses exactly two sizes: the first sentence large and bold, everything after it small and regular. The split happens at the first `.`, `!`, `?` or `।`.

rules.name: The Indic Line Rule
rules.body: Line heights are always explicit (about 1.3 to 1.45x) with trimming off, so Devanagari matras and Dravidian vowel signs are never clipped and a two-line instruction never falls apart into two lines. Pill words shrink to fit (to 13sp) rather than truncate.

rules.name: The Light Veil Rule
rules.body: The app underneath is dimmed, never blacked out (22% by day, 32% at night), so the senior still recognises their own screen.

dos: Do retain native iPhone Form/navigation, pickers, SF Symbols, semantic `UIColor.label` text and Dynamic Type; keep white text, symbols and loading foreground on the blue prominent action.
Do retain standalone iPhone status when no next-step caption exists, and label Simulator guidance as synthetic.
Do use Bob as the product label and the shared authored lowercase b for the logo, with one clear open counter on the existing flat blue.
Do keep blue for where to press and what can be pressed: hand, spotlight halo, Help pill, primary pill, selected tile.
Do float the caption at the top below the status bar, and move it to the bottom only when it would cover the target.
Do keep the Help pill against a screen edge and move it to the other side when it comes within 24dp of the target.
Do split every caption into a large bold first sentence and a smaller 70%-white remainder.
Do make every pressable control a full pill at least 56dp tall.
Do pair every state colour with a drawn glyph or word (tick, lock, warning, voice bars, arc).
Do draw icons from the shared 24-unit glyph set with its one rounded stroke; never mix in an icon font.
Do set explicit line heights for Indic scripts and shrink pill words to fit instead of truncating.
Do honour "Remove animations": the hand flight, nod and pulses become instant cuts.
donts: Don't imply that iPhone has Android overlays, pointer motion or automatic actions; native grouped controls are the scoped adaptation.
Don't replace the lowercase b with an uppercase B, a font glyph or the generated concept raster, or add a gradient to its background.
Don't build bordered signboards, edge bands or boxy outline buttons; the caption is a borderless floating card.
Don't put grey panels, tints or colour inside the caption card; it stays white on near-black.
Don't dim the app heavily; the veil stays at 22% by day and 32% at night.
Don't let the hand body or the Help pill sit over the next row or the target; the tip rests inside the target.
Don't use colour alone for any state, selection or warning.
Don't put more than one primary pill on a setup step.
